assessments.skill: Your first local HTTP lab
assessments.experiment: Serve one page on your own computer, request it with curl, then compare its successful response with a request for a page that does not exist.
assessments.variant: Repeat the local page request on port 8766. Predict which part of the URL must change, then record the actual response.
assessments.control: Stop your local server and repeat the same request. Explain why a connection failure differs from an HTTP 404 returned by a running server.
assessments.recall: Without opening the walkthrough, explain 127.0.0.1, a port, a GET request, HTTP 200, HTTP 404 and a connection failure.

assessments.skill: What authorizes this test?
assessments.experiment: Read scenario.json. Write scope.md naming Harbor Notes, 127.0.0.1:8765, the two synthetic users alice and bob, and the permitted GET requests. Mira is the fictional service owner and Dev is the stop/escalation contact.
assessments.variant: Add a third-party login dependency and decide which requests must remain excluded until permission changes.
assessments.control: Show a technically reachable endpoint that the written scope forbids, and leave it untouched.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct the difference between technical access, ownership and authorization.

assessments.skill: Follow a hypothesis, not a tool list
assessments.experiment: Start service.py in Terminal A. In Terminal B, inventory its response and read its three endpoint handlers in the source.
assessments.variant: Move the app to a new port or change a visible header and revise the hypotheses using actual behavior.
assessments.control: Compare a real route with an intentionally nonexistent route so a generic error page is not counted as a finding.
assessments.recall: Given a new banner, name the next observation that could disprove your hypothesis.

assessments.skill: Two accounts, one boundary
assessments.experiment: Use the local service.py fixture. Note 1 belongs to alice; note 2 belongs to bob. Read do_GET and predict owner and cross-user results.
assessments.variant: Change the object or HTTP method and predict whether the authorization decision should change.
assessments.control: Demonstrate legitimate owner access and a denied unauthorized request on a corrected local equivalent.
assessments.recall: Explain why hiding a button is different from enforcing authorization.

assessments.skill: Inspect and narrow permissions on a local file
assessments.experiment: Use Linux, macOS or WSL for this filesystem exercise. Work only on the extracted permissions.txt file. Inspect your identity and its mode.
assessments.variant: Change the training file to 640 and compare owner/group/other bits with 600. Record what a second-identity test would be needed to verify.
assessments.control: Owner reading must still work; do not claim a runtime test as another user if you only inspected mode bits.
assessments.recall: Explain the difference between authentication, authorization and process privilege.

assessments.skill: Make a finding another person can verify
assessments.experiment: Use your saved owner/cross-user test from web-boundaries. Name the fixture version ascend-notes-v1 and the exact note/user relationship.
assessments.variant: Give a peer a changed input or repeat on a second clean fixture and identify assumptions missing from the report.
assessments.control: Show that the fix rejects the bad case without breaking an ordinary valid request.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct a finding from its root cause without copying the original prose.

assessments.skill: Run a small authorized assessment
assessments.experiment: Extract a fresh copy of service.py and scenario.json. Independently use note 2 (owner bob) and alice as the unrelated user. State the scope before starting.
assessments.variant: Change an account role or route and independently reassess whether the suspected weakness remains.
assessments.control: Include an out-of-scope action you deliberately excluded and a benign workflow that survives the repair.
assessments.recall: Explain the assessment chain, one false lead and what evidence changed your mind.

assessments.skill: Recheck the boundary with a specified change
assessments.experiment: Use note 2 and replace its owner with carol in a fresh service.py copy. Update only the list of recognized synthetic users needed for that identity, then independently test and repair ownership.
assessments.variant: Add a second case by reversing the changed condition above, predict its result and compare actual behavior.
assessments.control: Bob must still read his own remaining test note; alice must not gain access to carol’s note.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct why the specified input change did or did not change the outcome. State help used and what remains untested.

assessments.skill: Create a harmless marker and verify cleanup
assessments.experiment: Observe the difference between performing an action and collecting evidence of it.
assessments.variant: In a new copy, change the marker filename to training-marker-2.txt and predict which event fields should change. Run and compare.
assessments.control: Delete the remove step only in a disposable COPY. Verify that a remaining marker is a cleanup failure, not evidence of successful cleanup.
assessments.recall: Without opening your report, reconstruct the inputs, observed result and main limitation of create a harmless marker and verify cleanup.

assessments.skill: Measure an objective, not a shell
assessments.experiment: Read context.json and marker.py. Write an engagement plan limited to creation and deletion of this local marker; use Mira and Dev as the fictional owner/defender contacts.
assessments.variant: Add an operational constraint such as unavailable endpoint logging and redesign the objective or telemetry plan honestly.
assessments.control: Show a scenario that appears successful technically but fails the stated business objective.
assessments.recall: State the difference between a penetration-test finding and an adversary-emulation objective.

assessments.skill: Choose techniques from evidence
assessments.experiment: Read the linked ATT&CK T1074.001 description (local data staging). Define a hypothesis that creating a named harmless local file could produce observable file events.
assessments.variant: Replace the assumed identity or endpoint type and remove techniques whose prerequisites no longer hold.
assessments.control: Include one plausible but unsupported technique and explain why it was excluded.
assessments.recall: Rebuild the evidence-to-technique chain and name its uncertainty.

assessments.skill: Know what the defender can see
assessments.experiment: Run marker.py once in a fresh extracted folder and open marker-events.jsonl alongside events.csv.
assessments.variant: Change the marker path or process argument and predict which detection features remain stable.
assessments.control: Repeat an ordinary administration action and distinguish its evidence from the staged behavior.
assessments.recall: Explain which sensor would be needed to resolve a missing observation.

assessments.skill: Make a small emulation reversible
assessments.experiment: Use the marker-only plan from objectives. Read the exact marker.py copy you intend to run and record its hash with python3 -m hashlib only if available; otherwise use sha256sum marker.py on Linux.
assessments.variant: Change a nonessential filename or account context and predict whether the intended behavior is still observable.
assessments.control: Verify the artifact did not exist before, appears during the test, and is absent after cleanup; preserve unrelated files.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct the prerequisites and rollback steps without running a script blindly.

assessments.skill: Test detection with a partner
assessments.experiment: Combine a COPY of events.csv with the two marker events into a table whose columns include source, time, action and evidence ID. Keep source differences visible.
assessments.variant: Change a superficial indicator while preserving behavior and retest the revised analytic.
assessments.control: Include an administration lookalike that should remain unalerted or receive a documented lower-confidence classification.
assessments.recall: Explain why a detection that matches only the demonstration filename is fragile.

assessments.skill: Deliver a defensible exercise report
assessments.experiment: Use a new folder and your approved marker plan. Predict creation, logging and cleanup for training-marker-2.txt.
assessments.variant: Withhold one assumed permission or telemetry source and adapt the plan without exceeding scope.
assessments.control: Demonstrate reset to baseline and distinguish untested coverage from a demonstrated miss.
assessments.recall: Explain what the exercise supports about defensive readiness and what it cannot establish.

assessments.skill: Recheck the boundary with a specified change
assessments.experiment: In a fresh marker.py copy, omit the deletion log while retaining deletion itself. Determine whether you can establish cleanup from filesystem inspection and which telemetry is missing.
assessments.variant: Add a second case by reversing the changed condition above, predict its result and compare actual behavior.
assessments.control: Retain the creation event and confirm that missing telemetry is not evidence that the action never happened.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct why the specified input change did or did not change the outcome. State help used and what remains untested.

assessments.skill: Read a login timeline in two time zones
assessments.experiment: Find the same user’s events without confusing local time with UTC.
assessments.variant: Change only e3 to the equivalent UTC timestamp in a copy; the normalized timeline should be unchanged.
assessments.control: Use alice-test and e7 as exclusions; a substring match or an unbounded time query must not include them.
assessments.recall: Without opening your report, reconstruct the inputs, observed result and main limitation of read a login timeline in two time zones.

assessments.skill: Turn an alert into a question
assessments.experiment: Use events.csv, context.json and message.eml. Create three queue items: Alice’s failures followed by role change; Bob’s blocked web link; the backup maintenance login.
assessments.variant: Change an asset from a sandbox to a critical service and justify whether prioritization changes.
assessments.control: Keep a noisy but low-impact event from outranking a corroborated compromise solely because of event volume.
assessments.recall: Explain event, alert, incident, severity and confidence using one example.

assessments.skill: Follow the entity across logs
assessments.experiment: Use the foundations timestamp-normalization command as a starting point. Filter exact user alice and the inclusive 09:00–09:10 UTC window; print id, time, host and source_ip.
assessments.variant: Change the time zone or host identifier in a synthetic copy and adjust the query without losing the same activity.
assessments.control: Include a similarly named account and an event outside the window that must not be joined.
assessments.recall: Recreate the query logic from the investigation question rather than memorizing syntax.

assessments.skill: Investigate a suspicious sign-in
assessments.experiment: Review e1–e4 and e11 in events.csv with context.json. Distinguish failed login, successful login, allowed role change and denied administrator grant.
assessments.variant: Add a service-account explanation or a contradictory device event and update the conclusion.
assessments.control: Include known maintenance logins and avoid treating location or failure count alone as compromise.
assessments.recall: Explain which evidence would raise or lower confidence in account misuse.

assessments.skill: Preserve evidence before following a lure
assessments.experiment: Read message.eml as TEXT. The .invalid URL is inert; there is no attachment to run. Correlate its Date and recipient with events e9 and e10.
assessments.variant: Change a redirect or add a blocked request and reassess how far the activity progressed.
assessments.control: Include a legitimate message with similar wording and a blocked attempt with no evidence of execution.
assessments.recall: Explain why receipt, click, execution and compromise are separate claims.

assessments.skill: Make containment proportionate
assessments.experiment: Write response.md for the fictional Alice case. Before containment, preserve a copy of events.csv and its SHA-256 hash; no real account should be changed.
assessments.variant: Make the affected system unavailable to the responder and choose an alternative action with explicit residual risk.
assessments.control: Show that an unrelated account or service still works after containment.
assessments.recall: State the evidence needed before choosing a disruptive action.

assessments.skill: Close the case so someone can reopen it
assessments.experiment: Use a fresh copy of events.csv. Ask a peer to change one identity/time field, or move e4 outside the window yourself and record that assistance.
assessments.variant: Add a late contradictory event and revise the disposition while retaining the earlier reasoning.
assessments.control: Document one rejected hypothesis and a known-benign comparison; do not turn missing logs into a clean bill of health.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct the case and next action from the handoff alone after a delay.

assessments.skill: Recheck the boundary with a specified change
assessments.experiment: Add a synthetic approval for e4 to context.json, then move e4 outside the original investigation window in events.csv. Reevaluate the Alice case using your saved query.
assessments.variant: Add a second case by reversing the changed condition above, predict its result and compare actual behavior.
assessments.control: Keep alice-test excluded and preserve the denied status of e11.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct why the specified input change did or did not change the outcome. State help used and what remains untested.

assessments.skill: Trace group membership in a small directory model
assessments.experiment: Predict a permission path before inspecting a real directory.
assessments.variant: Remove LabReaders from LabOperators in a copy and redraw the reachable group path.
assessments.control: Keep LabOperator in LabOperators. Explain why that unrelated membership should remain intact.
assessments.recall: Without opening your report, reconstruct the inputs, observed result and main limitation of trace group membership in a small directory model.

assessments.skill: Draw the domain before testing it
assessments.experiment: Prepare an isolated training.example.test forest using the linked Microsoft AD DS installation guide on a fresh evaluation VM. Point a separate training client’s DNS at the DC. Record the VM network, OS build and reset snapshot.
assessments.variant: Change the client DNS server in the disposable lab and predict which discovery or authentication step fails.
assessments.control: Compare a local login with a domain login and explain which identity authority answered.
assessments.recall: Recreate the domain discovery and trust boundaries from memory.

assessments.skill: A ticket is not a password
assessments.experiment: Use your joined training client and DC from domain-model. Record their clock/DNS settings. On the client run klist before and after accessing a share you created on the training DC.
assessments.variant: Change a service name or introduce documented clock skew in the disposable lab and predict the failure or fallback.
assessments.control: Include a normal successful service access and a deliberately invalid service reference.
assessments.recall: Explain why DNS, SPNs and time synchronization matter to Kerberos.

assessments.skill: Prove an identity graph edge
assessments.experiment: Create LabReaders and LabOperators groups in your isolated domain and place them under the Training OU. Recreate the nested membership in directory-model.json.
assessments.variant: Remove one group membership or inherited permission and predict whether the path still exists.
assessments.control: Include a graph edge that appears plausible but is denied by the effective permissions.
assessments.recall: Explain the distinction between a graph hypothesis and a verified authorization path.

assessments.skill: Separate management power from service identity
assessments.experiment: In Group Policy Management on your training DC, create an otherwise empty TrainingNotes GPO linked only to the Training OU. Record its scope and delegation tab.
assessments.variant: Restrict the policy link or delegated target and predict which administrative or service action stops working.
assessments.control: Keep an intended management action functioning after the proposed least-privilege change.
assessments.recall: Explain why controlling a policy object and applying that policy are separate conditions.

assessments.skill: Follow the certificate enrollment decision
assessments.experiment: This task additionally needs an isolated AD CS evaluation lab. Follow Microsoft AD CS installation documentation; take a reset snapshot before adding the role. Keep issued certificates in the training domain.
assessments.variant: Change enrollment rights or an identity-related template setting and predict which request is permitted or rejected.
assessments.control: Show a legitimate enrollment still works and an unauthorized identity request is rejected after the repair.
assessments.recall: Explain why possessing a valid certificate is not sufficient proof of an authorized identity.

assessments.skill: Harden a small domain and retest it
assessments.experiment: Use your existing training domain and a fresh test OU. Audit DNS discovery, one domain sign-in and one inherited permission or GPO delegation edge.
assessments.variant: Change one account's memberships or a policy scope and independently re-evaluate the affected path.
assessments.control: Retest normal user/service sign-in and document which enterprise controls were not present in the lab.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct one privilege path and the exact permission change that removed it.

assessments.skill: Recheck the boundary with a specified change
assessments.experiment: In your isolated domain, move the TrainingNotes GPO link from the Training OU to a new TrainingReview OU containing only LabOperator. Predict and measure which test user is affected.
assessments.variant: Add a second case by reversing the changed condition above, predict its result and compare actual behavior.
assessments.control: Normal LabReader sign-in must still work; leave other OUs untouched.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct why the specified input change did or did not change the outcome. State help used and what remains untested.

assessments.skill: Compare two roles in a local permission model
assessments.experiment: Read a concrete access matrix without needing a cloud subscription.
assessments.variant: Remove write from editor in a copy; predict and rerun the matrix.
assessments.control: Reader read must remain allowed, and unknown write must remain denied.
assessments.recall: Without opening your report, reconstruct the inputs, observed result and main limitation of compare two roles in a local permission model.

assessments.skill: Identify who owns each control
assessments.experiment: Use cloud.json as the fictional asset inventory. Name the notes resource, local region, application owner and provider/team responsibility split.
assessments.variant: Move one component from a VM to a managed service and revise the shared-responsibility assumptions.
assessments.control: Include a provider-managed control that a workload operator cannot fix by changing application code.
assessments.recall: Explain the difference between provider security and secure use of the provider.

assessments.skill: Predict the authorization decision
assessments.experiment: Run policy.py and write the reader/editor read/write matrix before changing it. Record the public flag separately from role permissions; this model does not apply the flag in its evaluator.
assessments.variant: Add a condition or a resource policy and predict how the effective decision changes.
assessments.control: Demonstrate a denied unrelated principal and an intended allowed operation.
assessments.recall: Explain why an identity policy alone may not determine effective access.

assessments.skill: Public does not always mean intended
assessments.experiment: Read cloud.json exposure and public fields. Define intended access: internet reaches the load-balancer only; notes is not publicly readable.
assessments.variant: Change a resource from private to shared-with-one-role and verify that the intended boundary survives.
assessments.control: Preserve legitimate client access and demonstrate that an unrelated identity cannot read the object.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct the layers required to explain one exposure finding.

assessments.skill: Separate workload identity from static keys
assessments.experiment: Implement a local token record with fields token_id, allowed_action, expires_at and revoked. Use fixed synthetic times so tests are reproducible; no real credentials.
assessments.variant: Change the audience, role or expiry and predict whether the request should still authenticate.
assessments.control: Verify a valid authorized request succeeds and a stale token is rejected without logging its contents.
assessments.recall: Explain rotation, revocation and short-lived identity as different mechanisms.

assessments.skill: Follow a control-plane change
assessments.experiment: Use cloud.json audit, where every event has a stable c-ID. Sort the grant/access sequence by event time and distinguish success from denied.
assessments.variant: Change a resource name or actor and test whether the behavioral analytic still finds the sequence.
assessments.control: Include a denied change and a known maintenance change that must not be labeled successful compromise.
assessments.recall: Explain what the audit source can and cannot establish about data access.

assessments.skill: Deliver a bounded cloud review
assessments.experiment: Make a fresh copy of cloud.json with resource id changed to project-notes and actor alice changed to trainee. Add a direct internet → project-notes edge.
assessments.variant: Change one trust policy or network boundary and independently reassess the affected access path.
assessments.control: Verify legitimate workload behavior and prove temporary lab resources were removed where a real account was used.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct the finding, provider-specific limits and remaining assurance gaps.

assessments.skill: Recheck the boundary with a specified change
assessments.experiment: In cloud.json rename notes to archive and remove editor write. Update the local policy/exposure tests to use the changed resource and intended read-only workflow.
assessments.variant: Add a second case by reversing the changed condition above, predict its result and compare actual behavior.
assessments.control: Reader read remains allowed and unknown write remains denied. State provider-specific behavior left untested.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct why the specified input change did or did not change the outcome. State help used and what remains untested.

assessments.skill: Inspect the process inside your first training container
assessments.experiment: Build a minimal local image and verify its runtime user.
assessments.variant: Override the training container user with --user 10002:10002 and compare id output.
assessments.control: Run with --network none and confirm identity inspection still works; network access is unnecessary for this check.
assessments.recall: Without opening your report, reconstruct the inputs, observed result and main limitation of inspect the process inside your first training container.

assessments.skill: A container still shares a kernel
assessments.experiment: Use the downloaded Dockerfile and build ascend-notes:training. Run id with --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges --read-only --tmpfs /tmp:rw,size=16m --network none.
assessments.variant: Remove one required write path or change its owner and predict which operation fails.
assessments.control: Preserve the service's intended request while showing it cannot write to an unrelated path.
assessments.recall: Explain which risks these controls reduce and which require stronger isolation.

assessments.skill: Know exactly which image ran
assessments.experiment: Build the Dockerfile and record docker image inspect output, including base image identity. Install a locally supported Syft release from its official documentation if using an SBOM generator.
assessments.variant: Resolve an updated tag and identify the changed digest and dependencies before accepting it.
assessments.control: Include a scanner finding for an unused or unreachable component and separate presence from demonstrated exploitability.
assessments.recall: Explain why a matching digest gives identity but not a guarantee of safety.

assessments.skill: Test an isolation claim
assessments.experiment: Pull nginx:alpine for this network task; unlike service.py it listens on the container interface. Run a named disposable container with --memory 128m --cpus 0.5 --pids-limit 64 and -p 127.0.0.1:8765:80.
assessments.variant: Move the client to another lab network and predict which target it should fail to reach.
assessments.control: Confirm a permitted same-network request works while cross-network and outbound probes fail within bounded timeouts.
assessments.recall: Explain what an internal bridge blocks and why the host kernel is still shared.

assessments.skill: Give the workload only its job
assessments.experiment: Create a disposable kind/minikube cluster using the linked setup guide; verify kubectl config current-context identifies that lab. Read pod.yaml, then apply it only there.
assessments.variant: Change the namespace or requested verb and predict the decision before checking.
assessments.control: Keep the intended read working and deny writes to unrelated secrets or namespaces.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct the subject, role and binding needed for one API permission.

assessments.skill: Observe enforcement, not just YAML
assessments.experiment: Use a disposable cluster whose CNI supports NetworkPolicy. Create an ascend-lab namespace, an nginx server pod/service and a curl client; record the image versions.
assessments.variant: Change one pod label or allowed port and predict which connection changes.
assessments.control: Include a matching permitted client and an unmatched client that must be denied; report an unsupported CNI as an unmet prerequisite.
assessments.recall: Explain why a valid NetworkPolicy object can coexist with unrestricted traffic.

assessments.skill: Review and repair a workload deployment
assessments.experiment: Use a copy of pod.yaml. Add an excessive pods/delete verb to its role as the deliberate configuration defect, then apply only in your disposable cluster.
assessments.variant: Change a namespace, image version or writable path and revise the controls instead of copying the old manifest.
assessments.control: Show an unrelated workload and legitimate client remain functional after the fix.
assessments.recall: Explain one runtime observation that would invalidate your review conclusion.

assessments.skill: Recheck the boundary with a specified change
assessments.experiment: In a disposable cluster, change the downloaded Role/RoleBinding namespace from ascend-lab to ascend-review and test the same service-account get/list/delete matrix there.
assessments.variant: Add a second case by reversing the changed condition above, predict its result and compare actual behavior.
assessments.control: The training service account must not gain privileges in default; delete only the new training namespace afterward.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct why the specified input change did or did not change the outcome. State help used and what remains untested.

assessments.skill: Run and inspect a tiny notes service
assessments.experiment: Make one real HTTP request and find its handler in source.
assessments.variant: Request /notes/2 as bob and trace that record in NOTES.
assessments.control: Request an unknown note; observe a 404 without treating it as an application crash.
assessments.recall: Without opening your report, reconstruct the inputs, observed result and main limitation of run and inspect a tiny notes service.

assessments.skill: Draw the trust boundary before coding
assessments.experiment: Use scenario.json and service.py. Draw browser → handler → in-memory notes and label X-Lab-User as a fake identity boundary.
assessments.variant: Add a background worker or third-party integration and revise the boundaries and threats.
assessments.control: Include a failure outside the service's responsibility and document the dependency instead of claiming to fix it.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct one threat from asset through entry point to consequence.

assessments.skill: Follow untrusted data to its sink
assessments.experiment: Use PATCH /notes/1 with X-Lab-User: alice and a small JSON body. Compare an intended text update with an attempted owner or internal-field update in the disposable fixture.
assessments.variant: Change the input encoding or rendering context and update the defense rather than reusing an unrelated escaping rule.
assessments.control: Include valid punctuation and an invalid structured input; reject the dangerous case without silently corrupting legitimate data.
assessments.recall: Explain why validation and output encoding address different boundaries.

assessments.skill: Put authorization beside the resource
assessments.experiment: Reproduce GET /notes/1 as bob, then add the missing owner check in do_GET.
assessments.variant: Add a new HTTP method or background operation and check that it enforces the same resource policy.
assessments.control: Keep owner access working and deny an authenticated but unauthorized user.
assessments.recall: State the policy independently of route names or UI controls.

assessments.skill: Make a dependency decision you can defend
assessments.experiment: Inventory this standard-library-only service: Python interpreter version, base OS if containerized, and no third-party runtime packages. Record those facts rather than inventing pip dependencies.
assessments.variant: Introduce a version change in a branch and assess both security and compatibility effects before merging.
assessments.control: Include an advisory that does not apply to the used component/version and explain the evidence.
assessments.recall: Explain why dependency presence, reachability and exploitability are separate claims.

assessments.skill: Make the pipeline stop for a real defect
assessments.experiment: Use unittest discovery for your authorization/property tests and a local script checking for a synthetic literal named TRAINING_SECRET_DO_NOT_COMMIT. Keep real credentials out.
assessments.variant: Change a fixture's filename or encoding and test whether the intended check still applies.
assessments.control: Confirm clean code builds successfully and no test prints secret-like fixture values into published logs.
assessments.recall: Explain the failure mode each gate detects and one it misses.

assessments.skill: Ship a small service with an assurance record
assessments.experiment: Commit the fixed local service, tests and version manifest in your training Git repo. Run the complete local test suite from a fresh copy.
assessments.variant: Change a dependency or deployment setting and rerun only the checks whose assumptions changed, explaining the choice.
assessments.control: Reproduce a known security regression on the old version and show the release rejects it while valid use works.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct the assurance argument and the strongest remaining limitation.

assessments.skill: Recheck the boundary with a specified change
assessments.experiment: Add a maximum text length of 80 to your fixed service. Test boundary lengths 79, 80 and 81 together with the cross-user and property-injection cases.
assessments.variant: Add a second case by reversing the changed condition above, predict its result and compare actual behavior.
assessments.control: A valid owner update remains usable; length validation must not replace ownership checks.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct why the specified input change did or did not change the outcome. State help used and what remains untested.

assessments.skill: Hash an evidence copy without changing the original
assessments.experiment: Preserve an authored file and distinguish content integrity from provenance.
assessments.variant: Edit only analysis-copy/note.txt and recalculate both hashes.
assessments.control: Verify the original hash stayed unchanged; differing copy bytes must not be described as an untouched original.
assessments.recall: Without opening your report, reconstruct the inputs, observed result and main limitation of hash an evidence copy without changing the original.

assessments.skill: Keep the original evidence original
assessments.experiment: Use original/ and the analysis-copy made in foundations. Record source description, acquisition field, hashes and your copy operation in a manifest.
assessments.variant: Change the copy or filename and determine which identity assertions still hold.
assessments.control: Include a corrupted copy that must fail integrity verification and a byte-identical renamed copy that must pass content verification.
assessments.recall: Explain integrity, provenance and chain of custody as different properties.

assessments.skill: Recover a story from file metadata
assessments.experiment: Use an analysis copy of original/note.txt. Inspect Path.stat() values for size, mtime and ctime; record your OS/filesystem semantics.
assessments.variant: Change the timezone display or introduce a copied file whose timestamps differ from its real acquisition time.
assessments.control: Include metadata that cannot prove who created a file and explicitly withhold that conclusion.
assessments.recall: Explain why one timestamp does not prove an event happened at that exact time.

assessments.skill: Reconcile clocks before drawing conclusions
assessments.experiment: Use events.csv and context.json. Normalize every timestamp to UTC and sort by event time, retaining row IDs and source filename.
assessments.variant: Add a clock-skew correction or delayed event and revise the ordering where justified.
assessments.control: Keep an unrelated similarly named process out of the incident chain.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct which event ordering is certain and which depends on clock assumptions.

assessments.skill: Separate a process artifact from a verdict
assessments.experiment: Download the named cridex.vmem training image via the Volatility Foundation Memory Samples page: https://github.com/volatilityfoundation/volatility/wiki/Memory-Samples . It is a memory image from a historical Windows malware investigation, not an executable to run. Check source terms, compressed/uncompressed size and hash before downloading.
assessments.variant: Change the filter or investigate a second process and independently test the same hypothesis.
assessments.control: Include a benign process with a suspicious-looking name and avoid treating its name alone as malware proof.
assessments.recall: Explain how an incompatible symbol profile can invalidate an apparently plausible result.

assessments.skill: Preserve the question while containing the risk
assessments.experiment: Use copies of events.csv and context.json for a tabletop response. Hash and preserve original logs before making a decision about fictional alice.
assessments.variant: Remove access to one evidence source and revise the plan without inventing missing facts.
assessments.control: Preserve a legitimate user's access and document evidence lost because of the chosen intervention.
assessments.recall: Explain one containment tradeoff and how it changes later interpretation.

assessments.skill: Deliver an evidence-led incident report
assessments.experiment: Create a variation of events.csv by moving e4 after the investigation window and changing one host. Preserve the changed input and disclose whether you or a peer selected it.
assessments.variant: Introduce one contradictory artifact and revise the explanation while retaining an audit of the earlier hypothesis.
assessments.control: Identify one tempting conclusion that the available evidence does not support.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct the case from the evidence index and independently recheck one claim.

assessments.skill: Recheck the boundary with a specified change
assessments.experiment: Add a synthetic device record contradicting the host attributed to e4 in your copied evidence bundle. Rebuild the timeline and state whether the join remains justified.
assessments.variant: Add a second case by reversing the changed condition above, predict its result and compare actual behavior.
assessments.control: Keep original evidence unchanged and retain its hashes; a conflicting record does not license deleting the earlier evidence.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct why the specified input change did or did not change the outcome. State help used and what remains untested.

assessments.skill: Separate event facts from a hunt hypothesis
assessments.experiment: Use a small log bundle to write a testable question.
assessments.variant: Add an approval note for e4 in a COPY of context.json and revise confidence.
assessments.control: Keep the denied e11 event as denied; do not count it as a successful administrator grant.
assessments.recall: Without opening your report, reconstruct the inputs, observed result and main limitation of separate event facts from a hunt hypothesis.

assessments.skill: Put confidence beside the claim
assessments.experiment: Use the ATT&CK Valid Accounts page as a public behavior reference and context.json as the synthetic local source. Record authorship, date accessed and collection limits separately.
assessments.variant: Add a conflicting source or newer report and explain which claims change.
assessments.control: Include a widely repeated claim without primary evidence and keep it below corroborated facts.
assessments.recall: Explain how source reliability differs from confidence in an individual claim.

assessments.skill: Turn a report into a huntable hypothesis
assessments.experiment: Define a hypothesis over events.csv: a successful role change followed by same-user resource access within five minutes deserves review.
assessments.variant: Change the assumed platform or available sensor and revise or reject the hypothesis.
assessments.control: Show a technique mapping that is too broad to justify the proposed query.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct the hypothesis without using an indicator list.

assessments.skill: Search for behavior through the noise
assessments.experiment: Write a Python csv/datetime query implementing your hypothesis with exact identity, bounded time and successful result. Use the foundations timeline normalization method.
assessments.variant: Change filenames, addresses or usernames while preserving behavior and evaluate coverage.
assessments.control: Include an ordinary administration sequence with similar individual events.
assessments.recall: Explain the false-positive mechanism of the original query.

assessments.skill: Enrich without inventing attribution
assessments.experiment: Use events.csv addresses and context.json to build a graph of user → host → synthetic source IP. Every edge needs a row ID, timestamp and confidence.
assessments.variant: Introduce a shared hosting address or recycled domain and remove unjustified relationships.
assessments.control: Demonstrate that shared infrastructure alone does not establish a common operator.
assessments.recall: Explain one edge that is useful operationally but insufficient for attribution.

assessments.skill: Exchange the meaning, not just the fields
assessments.experiment: Create a STIX 2.1 bundle for a fictional observed sequence using https://oasis-open.github.io/cti-documentation/ . Include a valid bundle UUID and an indicator with reserved-domain/IP data only.
assessments.variant: Update an observation or revoke an indicator and express the change without silently erasing its history.
assessments.control: Include a malformed relationship or unsupported claim that validation/review must reject.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct the difference between an observable, an indicator and an incident claim.

assessments.skill: Turn a hunt into an operational decision
assessments.experiment: Use a changed copy of events.csv with an additional approved maintenance role change. Keep expected labels separate.
assessments.variant: Add a changed positive sequence or remove a source and revise the result transparently.
assessments.control: Keep absence of evidence separate from proof that the behavior never occurred.
assessments.recall: Explain what action the hunt supports and what further collection is needed.

assessments.skill: Recheck the boundary with a specified change
assessments.experiment: Remove the role-change source rows from a COPY of events.csv. Rerun your successful-grant-followed-by-access hunt and revise the coverage statement.
assessments.variant: Add a second case by reversing the changed condition above, predict its result and compare actual behavior.
assessments.control: Do not report no matches as proof that no role change occurred; preserve the known benign maintenance context.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct why the specified input change did or did not change the outcome. State help used and what remains untested.

assessments.skill: Inspect a benign program before running it
assessments.experiment: Separate source capability, file identity and actual output.
assessments.variant: Change only the branch string in a new copy and predict the two outputs.
assessments.control: Use an unmatched input to verify that the marker branch is not always taken.
assessments.recall: Without opening your report, reconstruct the inputs, observed result and main limitation of inspect a benign program before running it.

assessments.skill: Describe the file before naming a family
assessments.experiment: Use sample.py and its SHA-256. Record file type as Python text, byte length, imports and embedded CONFIG string.
assessments.variant: Change compiler options or append harmless data and determine which identifiers and structural properties change.
assessments.control: Include a packed-looking or high-entropy benign file and avoid classifying it as malicious solely from entropy.
assessments.recall: Explain what a hash, import and string can each establish.

assessments.skill: Trace a benign Python branch in bytecode
assessments.experiment: Disassemble the choose function using python3 -c "import sample, dis; dis.dis(sample.choose)". Record Python version since bytecode changes by release.
assessments.variant: Change the input or compile optimization and re-identify the controlling condition.
assessments.control: Include an unreachable suspicious-looking string that does not prove execution.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct the condition-to-effect chain without searching for keywords.

assessments.skill: Investigate a trace without executing a sample
assessments.experiment: Open trace.json, which is explicitly synthetic telemetry. Build a timeline retaining b-IDs and distinguish sample stdout from the analyst shell’s file redirection.
assessments.variant: Add a failed operation or contradictory timestamp and revise the behavior claims.
assessments.control: Include an attempted connection that never succeeded and avoid calling it confirmed data transfer.
assessments.recall: Explain one gap that would require a different sensor or controlled VM analysis.

assessments.skill: Decode only what the evidence supports
assessments.experiment: Locate CONFIG in sample.py and decode it with base64 into bytes, then json.loads. Preserve the original encoded string and its byte offset in the file.
assessments.variant: Change key order, length or encoding and make the parser fail clearly or support the documented variation.
assessments.control: Include a malformed/truncated fixture that must not yield a fabricated valid configuration.
assessments.recall: Explain why successful decoding is not equivalent to execution or attribution.

assessments.skill: Write a rule that survives a renamed file
assessments.experiment: Create three source copies: unchanged sample.py, a copy with a harmless whitespace edit, and a benign unrelated hello-world file. Record hashes as the sample set.
assessments.variant: Rename or recompile the toy sample and evaluate which features survive.
assessments.control: Include unrelated binaries sharing a common string so an overbroad signature fails the assessment.
assessments.recall: Explain one expected false positive and how to investigate it.

assessments.skill: Present a defensible analysis, not a label
assessments.experiment: Use a fresh sample.py copy with changed CONFIG topic and branch string. Keep source, disassembly, run output and the synthetic trace separately identified.
assessments.variant: Change one fixture property or trace event and independently revise the affected conclusion.
assessments.control: Demonstrate a claim you deliberately withheld because the artifact or trace was insufficient.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct the strongest finding and the observation that could disprove it.

assessments.skill: Recheck the boundary with a specified change
assessments.experiment: Change sample.py CONFIG topic and branch literal in a fresh copy without consulting the prior report. Recover fields, predict both branches and retest your signature.
assessments.variant: Add a second case by reversing the changed condition above, predict its result and compare actual behavior.
assessments.control: A hello-world file must remain a non-match. State that native binaries and unknown malware were not analyzed.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct why the specified input change did or did not change the outcome. State help used and what remains untested.

assessments.skill: Read an Android manifest and state its limits
assessments.experiment: Identify exposed components in a synthetic app declaration.
assessments.variant: In a copy, add a caller permission to the provider and predict what external callers would need.
assessments.control: Keep the main activity launchable in your design; blanket removal of every component is not a useful repair.
assessments.recall: Without opening your report, reconstruct the inputs, observed result and main limitation of read an android manifest and state its limits.

assessments.skill: Locate the mobile trust boundary
assessments.experiment: Choose the OWASP MASTG Hacking Playground Android app from the linked test-app index; follow that app’s README to build/install it on your own emulator. Record APK hash, OS/API level and package name.
assessments.variant: Add an exported component or a new permission in a toy build and reassess exposure.
assessments.control: Include a permission declaration that does not establish actual sensitive behavior by itself.
assessments.recall: Explain how platform permissions and backend authorization differ.

assessments.skill: Find where the app leaves data
assessments.experiment: On your practice app/emulator, choose a documented storage lesson and create a unique synthetic value such as ASCEND_TRAINING_NOTE. Record the exact lesson and app build.
assessments.variant: Change device state or storage location and predict whether the same extraction method applies.
assessments.control: Keep intended app persistence working and show that unrelated sandboxed apps do not gain access through the proposed fix.
assessments.recall: Explain encryption-at-rest limits when the app itself can access the key.

assessments.skill: Inspect a request without weakening the conclusion
assessments.experiment: Use only a documented network lesson in the OWASP practice app. Configure a debugging proxy on your emulator following the app’s instructions; use synthetic values only.
assessments.variant: Change the server certificate or hostname and predict acceptance or rejection.
assessments.control: Verify a valid connection succeeds and an invalid identity is rejected by the corrected toy app.
assessments.recall: Explain why disabling pinning for analysis does not prove a production bypass.

assessments.skill: Test the component's actual caller
assessments.experiment: Select one documented exported-component lesson in the practice app. Record component name, calling test app/adb identity and required permission.
assessments.variant: Change a deep-link parameter or invoking app identity and predict whether access should be permitted.
assessments.control: Keep the intended navigation working while rejecting an unauthorized or malformed invocation.
assessments.recall: Explain why an exported component is a review target rather than automatically a vulnerability.

assessments.skill: The phone is not the authorization boundary
assessments.experiment: Use local service.py independently of the Android UI. Compare alice and bob requesting /notes/1 with curl; the fake header simulates identity for the boundary exercise.
assessments.variant: Change object ID or request method and repeat the authorization decision with fresh evidence.
assessments.control: Preserve authorized access and deny an authenticated user who does not own the resource.
assessments.recall: Explain which finding belongs to the mobile client and which belongs to the backend.

assessments.skill: Deliver a platform-aware mobile review
assessments.experiment: Choose a second documented lesson in the same practice APK, different from your previous one. Record its MASTG objective, APK version and emulator state.
assessments.variant: Change an OS/app version or component permission and independently re-evaluate the affected finding.
assessments.control: Record a test whose result depends on debug/rooted-device conditions and limit the production claim accordingly.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct one finding including the exact platform assumptions required to reproduce it.

assessments.skill: Recheck the boundary with a specified change
assessments.experiment: In an owned build of your selected OWASP practice-app component lesson, add a caller permission to the test component. Compare before/after behavior from authorized and unrelated test callers.
assessments.variant: Add a second case by reversing the changed condition above, predict its result and compare actual behavior.
assessments.control: The intended app workflow must still work. Without an owned build/emulator, leave the runtime task incomplete.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct why the specified input change did or did not change the outcome. State help used and what remains untested.

assessments.skill: Compare authentication and ownership in a local API
assessments.experiment: Use two synthetic identities against one concrete note.
assessments.variant: Use note 2 with its owner bob and unrelated alice.
assessments.control: A request without X-Lab-User should not return note contents.
assessments.recall: Without opening your report, reconstruct the inputs, observed result and main limitation of compare authentication and ownership in a local api.

assessments.skill: Find the contract the client assumes
assessments.experiment: Read service.py and inventory GET /health, GET /notes/{id} and PATCH /notes/{id}; list inputs, outputs and fake identity handling.
assessments.variant: Add a deprecated route or alternate version and update the inventory and risk assumptions.
assessments.control: Distinguish an intentionally public endpoint from an unintentionally unprotected operation.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct one API trust boundary from method, identity and object.

assessments.skill: Change the object, keep the identity
assessments.experiment: Use GET /notes/1 as alice and bob; save baseline status/body. Find where do_GET recognizes a user but omits ownership.
assessments.variant: Change the object type or HTTP verb and test whether the same boundary is enforced.
assessments.control: Show legitimate owner access and rejection of an unrelated authenticated user.
assessments.recall: Explain why unpredictable IDs cannot replace authorization.

assessments.skill: Who may write this field?
assessments.experiment: As alice, PATCH note 1 with text only and then owner set to bob in the resettable fixture. Record whether the source allows both; restart afterward.
assessments.variant: Nest the property or switch update methods and predict whether the policy should change.
assessments.control: Keep ordinary editable fields working while rejecting privileged field writes and suppressing private response fields.
assessments.recall: Explain the relationship between mass assignment and field-level authorization.

assessments.skill: Validate the whole token contract
assessments.experiment: This fixture has no real bearer-token authentication. Implement a separate token-context checker using synthetic claims: subject, issuer, audience, expiry and allowed action.
assessments.variant: Change audience, scope or expiry and predict which validation layer rejects the request.
assessments.control: Include a correctly signed but wrong-audience token and an authorized valid token.
assessments.recall: Explain why a valid signature does not make every action authorized.

assessments.skill: Make expensive work bounded
assessments.experiment: Inspect the existing 2048-byte PATCH bound. Test one short valid text body and one 2049-byte body with a single request each; no traffic flood is needed.
assessments.variant: Change nesting depth or batch composition and predict the work budget decision.
assessments.control: Preserve a legitimate paginated request and reject an inexpensive-looking input that exceeds the actual work budget.
assessments.recall: Explain why request count alone may not bound resource consumption.

assessments.skill: Test a workflow across its endpoints
assessments.experiment: Extract a new service.py copy and use note 2/bob for the owned case. Independently assess object access, mutable fields and response properties.
assessments.variant: Change operation order or user role and independently test whether the business invariant still holds.
assessments.control: Verify normal workflow completion and a rejected unauthorized transition after the fix.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct the finding from the business invariant rather than the endpoint name.

assessments.skill: Recheck the boundary with a specified change
assessments.experiment: In your repaired service, add note 3 owned by alice. Test text update then read, cross-user PATCH, and an attempt to change owner before a read.
assessments.variant: Add a second case by reversing the changed condition above, predict its result and compare actual behavior.
assessments.control: Bob must retain access to note 2, and changing operation order must not expose note 3.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct why the specified input change did or did not change the outcome. State help used and what remains untested.

assessments.skill: Round-trip bytes through two encodings
assessments.experiment: See which transformations are reversible without a secret.
assessments.variant: Add a zero byte to the message in a copy and predict how length and encoded output change.
assessments.control: Ensure your decode preserves the zero byte; text trimming is not a valid bytes round trip.
assessments.recall: Without opening your report, reconstruct the inputs, observed result and main limitation of round-trip bytes through two encodings.

assessments.skill: Bytes are not the text displaying them
assessments.experiment: Use message from bytes_lab.py. Write round-trip assertions for hex and base64, then include bytes 0 and 255 in a new message.
assessments.variant: Introduce a zero byte or non-ASCII character and predict the representation change.
assessments.control: Reject malformed encoded input and preserve a valid binary message exactly.
assessments.recall: Explain why encoding provides no confidentiality.

assessments.skill: A checksum does not authenticate its author
assessments.experiment: Using hmac from the standard library and the public training key, compute an HMAC-SHA256 tag for message. Verify with hmac.compare_digest.
assessments.variant: Change one message byte or use a different key and predict verification.
assessments.control: Accept the valid message and reject both tampering and a MAC made with the wrong key.
assessments.recall: Explain integrity versus origin authentication.

assessments.skill: Make misuse visible in a toy experiment
assessments.experiment: Create a separate virtual environment and install cryptography using its official installation instructions. Record version. Use AESGCM with a generated key and a fresh 12-byte random nonce.
assessments.variant: Change associated data or the nonce and predict which operation should fail.
assessments.control: Keep the valid round trip working and reject a changed tag without releasing plaintext.
assessments.recall: Explain the nonce-use rule of the selected algorithm.

assessments.skill: State exactly what a signature proves
assessments.experiment: Use cryptography Ed25519PrivateKey.generate, sign and the corresponding public_key().verify on a synthetic note.
assessments.variant: Change the message or trusted public key and predict the result.
assessments.control: Reject a valid signature from an untrusted key while accepting the intended signer's document.
assessments.recall: Explain why a signature alone does not establish a real-world identity.

assessments.skill: Test the certificate decision
assessments.experiment: Use openssl to create a one-day self-signed RSA training certificate with subject CN=localhost and subjectAltName=DNS:localhost; keep key/cert in this new lab folder. Start openssl s_server on 127.0.0.1:8443 with -www.
assessments.variant: Change the hostname or CA trust set and predict acceptance.
assessments.control: Demonstrate a valid connection and rejection of an unrelated trusted-but-wrong-host certificate.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct the checks needed for server identity validation.

assessments.skill: Find a protocol assumption that can be tested
assessments.experiment: Create a toy message envelope with payload, sender key identity, nonce and sequence number. Authenticate it with the standard-library HMAC exercise or the signature library.
assessments.variant: Reorder or replay a message and predict the corrected protocol's response.
assessments.control: Preserve a legitimate fresh exchange while rejecting a stale authenticated message.
assessments.recall: Explain which property the repair establishes and which it does not.

assessments.skill: Recheck the boundary with a specified change
assessments.experiment: Use your authenticated message envelope to send sequence 2 before sequence 1, then replay sequence 2. Define the intended ordering policy first and test it.
assessments.variant: Add a second case by reversing the changed condition above, predict its result and compare actual behavior.
assessments.control: A fresh permitted sequence must still be accepted; reject a stale authenticated replay for the stated reason.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct why the specified input change did or did not change the outcome. State help used and what remains untested.

assessments.skill: Identify a sensor’s data flow and trust boundary
assessments.experiment: Read one concrete IoT scenario before starting a broker.
assessments.variant: Change the desired topic to ascend/sensor/humidity and revise the access matrix.
assessments.control: A subscriber for temperature should not automatically get write permission to every sensor topic.
assessments.recall: Without opening your report, reconstruct the inputs, observed result and main limitation of identify a sensor’s data flow and trust boundary.

assessments.skill: Know which device and boundary you are testing
assessments.experiment: Use device.json as the documented simulation. Draw owner, device, broker, consumer and update source; mark every unauthenticated boundary.
assessments.variant: Add a companion cloud service and revise the data and trust boundaries.
assessments.control: Exclude unrelated nearby devices even when technically visible.
assessments.recall: Explain which observations require physical hardware.

assessments.skill: Follow a message through the broker
assessments.experiment: Start mosquitto -c broker.conf -v in Terminal A. In Terminal B subscribe with mosquitto_sub -h 127.0.0.1 -p 18883 -t ascend/sensor/temperature -C 1.
assessments.variant: Change the subscription wildcard and predict which messages are delivered.
assessments.control: Include an unmatched topic that must not reach the subscriber.
assessments.recall: Explain retained delivery versus a new live publication.

assessments.skill: Give each device only its topics
assessments.experiment: Copy broker.conf to a new local lab folder. Use mosquitto_passwd interactively to create publisher/subscriber TEST users and configure password_file with allow_anonymous false.
assessments.variant: Change a wildcard or identity and predict effective topic access.
assessments.control: Preserve a device's intended telemetry while denying another device's private topic.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct the difference between broker authentication and topic authorization.

assessments.skill: Inspect a synthetic Wi-Fi beacon
assessments.experiment: Open wifi-beacon.pcap from this track’s downloaded ZIP in Wireshark. This is an authored synthetic IEEE 802.11 beacon, not captured radio traffic; no adapter or account is needed.
assessments.variant: Compare wifi-beacon.pcap with http-training.pcap in the same ZIP. Name which address/control fields belong to each link type.
assessments.control: Identify a claim the one beacon cannot support, such as completed association or a captured handshake.
assessments.recall: Explain why a monitor-capable adapter is a prerequisite for some tests.

assessments.skill: Review update metadata in a device model
assessments.experiment: Use device.json firmware as a static metadata exercise. It explicitly contains no bootable image and no measured binary architecture. List version, signature state and provenance gaps.
assessments.variant: Change the model or version field and compare the toy predicate result. Keep the signature-verification stub clearly labeled.
assessments.control: Accept a matching newer update with a successful stub result; reject wrong-model, old-version and failed-signature inputs.
assessments.recall: Explain what static image analysis cannot prove about a running device.

assessments.skill: Review an end-to-end device workflow
assessments.experiment: Use your authenticated local broker configuration. In a new copy, introduce an overbroad subscriber write ACL, predict its effect and test with a harmless marker.
assessments.variant: Introduce another device identity or a changed topic layout and retest separation.
assessments.control: Keep legitimate telemetry working and deny the unrelated device.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct the finding through the complete device-to-service path.

assessments.skill: Recheck the boundary with a specified change
assessments.experiment: Add a second synthetic device identity and an ascend/sensor/humidity topic to your owned loopback broker. Independently write and test separate ACLs.
assessments.variant: Add a second case by reversing the changed condition above, predict its result and compare actual behavior.
assessments.control: The original temperature subscriber must retain its read and must not publish or access the humidity topic without a grant.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct why the specified input change did or did not change the outcome. State help used and what remains untested.

assessments.skill: Read a simulated tank register and state a safety constraint
assessments.experiment: Separate a numeric observation from an operational conclusion.
assessments.variant: Change register 10 to 65 in a copy and predict whether it falls outside the written range.
assessments.control: Read an unknown register in a small Python call and preserve the error; do not interpret missing data as a tank reading of zero.
assessments.recall: Without opening your report, reconstruct the inputs, observed result and main limitation of read a simulated tank register and state a safety constraint.

assessments.skill: Start with the process consequence
assessments.experiment: Use process.json to draw sensor, controller, operator display and historian as a fictional process. Mark the baseline peer and expected register read.
assessments.variant: Change a process dependency and revise the priority of affected controls.
assessments.control: Distinguish a confidentiality issue from a change that could affect safe operation.
assessments.recall: Explain why enterprise IT priorities cannot be copied blindly into OT.

assessments.skill: Read the register with its context
assessments.experiment: Use registers.py and traffic.csv. Map function 3 rows to the read-register concept and the function 6 row to a single-register write in the synthetic trace.
assessments.variant: Change register address or byte order in a fixture and predict the interpretation.
assessments.control: Reject an out-of-range or mismatched response instead of inventing a process value.
assessments.recall: Explain why a register number alone does not identify a physical measurement.

assessments.skill: Prove the permitted path
assessments.experiment: Define an offline allowlist using process.json baseline peer, function 3 and register 10. Implement a predicate over traffic.csv rows.
assessments.variant: Change a client role or destination port and predict whether access should remain.
assessments.control: Preserve required monitoring while denying an unrelated management path.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct one zone boundary and its operational justification.

assessments.skill: Distinguish a maintenance action from an anomaly
assessments.experiment: Use traffic.csv and process.json; keep the label column hidden while constructing a rule for unexpected peer or write function.
assessments.variant: Change a nonessential address or schedule and reassess the rule.
assessments.control: Include approved maintenance and record the context needed to avoid a false incident.
assessments.recall: Explain what the network sensor cannot establish about physical state.

assessments.skill: Rehearse a reversible change
assessments.experiment: Copy the register/traffic model before editing. Add a rule limiting reads to the baseline peer and preserve valid register 10 reads.
assessments.variant: Remove an assumed maintenance window and decide whether to defer or redesign the change.
assessments.control: Demonstrate that a failed validation leads to rollback rather than an unsupported success claim.
assessments.recall: Explain the evidence required before a change could be considered in a real plant.

assessments.skill: Run an incident tabletop with technical evidence
assessments.experiment: Use traffic.csv and process.json as the tabletop incident pack. Build a timeline for o1–o5 and identify the unexpected write/new peer.
assessments.variant: Add contradictory process evidence and revise the decision.
assessments.control: Reject an IT-style containment action that would violate the stated process constraint.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct the decision and the unresolved question requiring a process engineer.

assessments.skill: Recheck the boundary with a specified change
assessments.experiment: Add a second synthetic tank-level row at the same time as o4 with value 49 from a separate source. Revise your tabletop account and next evidence request.
assessments.variant: Add a second case by reversing the changed condition above, predict its result and compare actual behavior.
assessments.control: Do not disconnect the fictional operator network merely to make an IT containment checklist pass.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct why the specified input change did or did not change the outcome. State help used and what remains untested.

assessments.skill: Turn a service description into a bounded review
assessments.experiment: Identify what the service must protect and who makes its decisions.
assessments.variant: Reduce the restore target to two hours in a copy and reevaluate whether E1 meets it.
assessments.control: Do not reject the current service just because an unrelated design costs more; compare both against the same requirements.
assessments.recall: Without opening your report, reconstruct the inputs, observed result and main limitation of turn a service description into a bounded review.

assessments.skill: Define the system someone is responsible for
assessments.experiment: Use scenario.json components, owner and data. Draw a boundary around the service and identify any proposed outsourced component explicitly as a proposal.
assessments.variant: Add a new data recipient and revise ownership and control responsibilities.
assessments.control: Identify an asset outside the boundary that still creates a dependency risk.
assessments.recall: Explain why an incomplete boundary undermines an assessment.

assessments.skill: Connect the threat to a business consequence
assessments.experiment: Build risk-register.csv with three scenarios: cross-user reading, unauthorized note changes and loss of in-memory notes. Use E1/E2/source facts as evidence.
assessments.variant: Change exposure or business criticality and justify the resulting priority.
assessments.control: Avoid turning an unsupported numeric guess into a precise probability claim.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct one risk from cause to consequence.

assessments.skill: Make the control testable
assessments.experiment: Select NIST CSF outcomes relevant to access, detection and recovery. Record the exact outcome IDs from the current framework document.
assessments.variant: Change the hosting model and identify controls whose evidence must change.
assessments.control: Include a policy document that does not prove the operational control is running.
assessments.recall: Explain control design versus control operating effectiveness.

assessments.skill: Compare designs against explicit assumptions
assessments.experiment: Compare designs A and B in scenario.json against the same restore target, budget constraint and authorization threat model.
assessments.variant: Remove one assumed trusted component and revise the recommendation.
assessments.control: Document one risk accepted by the chosen design instead of claiming universal superiority.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct the tradeoff that drove the decision.

assessments.skill: Trace a requirement to its evidence
assessments.experiment: Review evidence E1 and E2 against today’s service requirements. Identify staleness, missing test coverage and scope mismatches.
assessments.variant: Change a requirement version or evidence date and reassess adequacy.
assessments.control: Reject a screenshot or scanner summary that cannot substantiate the actual claim.
assessments.recall: Explain the difference between a failed control and insufficient evidence.

assessments.skill: Deliver a decision-ready security review
assessments.experiment: Use a changed scenario with a two-hour restoration target and a missing owner for one component.
assessments.variant: Introduce a new dependency or material finding and update the decision transparently.
assessments.control: Keep a low-impact observation from obscuring an unresolved launch-critical control.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct the strongest assurance claim and its limits.

assessments.skill: Recheck the boundary with a specified change
assessments.experiment: Change the scenario restore target to two hours and add a dependency whose recovery time is six hours. Reevaluate designs A/B and the acceptance decision.
assessments.variant: Add a second case by reversing the changed condition above, predict its result and compare actual behavior.
assessments.control: Do not let a low-impact documentation improvement hide the unresolved recovery requirement.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct why the specified input change did or did not change the outcome. State help used and what remains untested.

assessments.skill: Check a finding against a deployed version
assessments.experiment: Separate a scan claim from evidence that the condition applies.
assessments.variant: Turn sharing off for asset A in a copy and rerun the checker.
assessments.control: Asset B on fixed version 1.1 must not be classified affected merely because a scan row names LAB-001.
assessments.recall: Without opening your report, reconstruct the inputs, observed result and main limitation of check a finding against a deployed version.

assessments.skill: Find the asset behind the finding
assessments.experiment: Join scan rows to assets by exact asset ID in inventory.json. Record component, version, owner, exposure and missing values.
assessments.variant: Rename a host or move a service and preserve its identity without merging unrelated assets.
assessments.control: Include two similar version strings that refer to different products.
assessments.recall: Explain why asset identity must precede prioritization.

assessments.skill: Is the advisory actually applicable?
assessments.experiment: Use the explicit LAB-001 condition: notes below 1.1 with sharing enabled. Evaluate A and B, then compare affected.py output.
assessments.variant: Change a required feature or version and revise applicability.
assessments.control: Include a matching product name with a nonaffected version.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct the conditions required before calling the finding applicable.

assessments.skill: Prioritize action using context
assessments.experiment: Use inventory.json exposure, criticality and fictional exploitation evidence. Apply a written SSVC-style decision path to each item.
assessments.variant: Change exposure or exploitation evidence and justify the revised action.
assessments.control: Include a high-score isolated lab finding and a lower-score exposed critical asset.
assessments.recall: Explain which new evidence would change the highest priority.

assessments.skill: Verify the repair rather than the ticket
assessments.experiment: In a COPY of inventory.json, model upgrading A to 1.1 or disabling sharing. Run affected.py before and after.
assessments.variant: Change the deployment variant and reassess whether the same mitigation applies.
assessments.control: Keep a ticket marked resolved from passing when the affected instance still has the old configuration.
assessments.recall: Explain patch presence versus effective remediation.

assessments.skill: Put an expiry date on accepted risk
assessments.experiment: Use fictional asset C as temporarily unpatchable because its owner/version is unresolved. Write an exception request with current uncertainty, decision owner and expiry.
assessments.variant: Remove a compensating control or change external exposure and reevaluate the exception.
assessments.control: Reject an indefinite exception without an accountable owner.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct when the exception must return to the remediation queue.

assessments.skill: Measure reduction in exposure
assessments.experiment: Use a new inventory copy where A is fixed and C now has an owner but still lacks a version.
assessments.variant: Add previously unknown assets and revise the metrics without hiding the changed denominator.
assessments.control: Distinguish a fall in scan coverage from a real reduction in exposure.
assessments.recall: Explain one metric that could look better while security became worse.

assessments.skill: Recheck the boundary with a specified change
assessments.experiment: Add a new exposed notes 1.0 asset D with sharing enabled to inventory.json but omit it from scan. Recompute known exposure and scan coverage.
assessments.variant: Add a second case by reversing the changed condition above, predict its result and compare actual behavior.
assessments.control: A smaller number of scan findings must not be reported as reduced exposure when coverage fell.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct why the specified input change did or did not change the outcome. State help used and what remains untested.

assessments.skill: Reproduce one boundary defect in an owned fixture
assessments.experiment: Find the smallest request pair that distinguishes intended from unintended access.
assessments.variant: Use note 2/bob as owner and alice as the unrelated identity.
assessments.control: A nonexistent object should give 404, not be counted as a successful unauthorized read.
assessments.recall: Without opening your report, reconstruct the inputs, observed result and main limitation of reproduce one boundary defect in an owned fixture.

assessments.skill: Treat program rules as part of the target
assessments.experiment: Use scenario.json scope and rate limit. Write a local-only research question about do_GET ownership or do_PATCH properties.
assessments.variant: Add an excluded third-party integration and revise the plan.
assessments.control: Identify a technically possible test that the scope disallows.
assessments.recall: Explain why a public bug-bounty page does not authorize every asset or technique.

assessments.skill: Find the invariant the software should preserve
assessments.experiment: Trace user input through the selected handler to the note read/update. Mark the exact missing or insufficient check.
assessments.variant: Change input encoding or operation order and predict the effect on the invariant.
assessments.control: Include a normal edge case that looks unusual but preserves the intended rule.
assessments.recall: Reconstruct the vulnerability hypothesis without relying on a scanner label.

assessments.skill: Make a small test generator teach you something
assessments.experiment: Use a bounded generator of at most 20 local cases over note IDs, missing identity and small JSON property names. One request per second; no arbitrary external URL input.
assessments.variant: Change the parser or seed corpus and verify the failure still tests the same property.
assessments.control: Include malformed input that is correctly rejected and must not count as a vulnerability.
assessments.recall: Explain crash, bug, security impact and exploitability as separate claims.

assessments.skill: Prove only the minimum necessary effect
assessments.experiment: Use only the synthetic note data. Show what one unrelated identity can read or alter and the prerequisites needed.
assessments.variant: Change the user role or object class and test whether the impact generalizes.
assessments.control: Include a failed unauthorized action and avoid claiming access merely from a different response size.
assessments.recall: Explain one stronger impact claim the evidence does not support.

assessments.skill: Write a report that survives first triage
assessments.experiment: Write a PRIVATE training report with title, affected local fixture/version, scope, minimal requests, actual output, impact limits and tested patch.
